## A portfolio built for feasible, evidence-driven theses

Sixteen public-data projects in four categories. Every project has a concrete task, a reproducible starting point, required baselines, an evaluation protocol and a scoped research contribution.

[Browse the projects](#portfolio-index){.btn .btn-primary} [Download the PDF](downloads/student-project-portfolio.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

## How the projects are structured

**Bachelor projects** emphasise implementation, fair comparison and one focused ablation. **Master projects** require a research question, a controlled methodological or protocol contribution, multi-seed evidence and a useful conclusion even when the proposed change does not improve average accuracy.

::: {.approved-callout}
**Integration assessment: approved with targeted corrections.** The four-category structure is academically coherent and feasible. Categories 1 and 2 preserve the Graph ML core, Category 3 adds a representation-learning strand, and Category 4 is intentionally narrow to keep foundation-model work within student compute budgets.
:::

## What counts as a Bachelor or Master contribution

| Dimension | Bachelor project | Master project |
|---|---|---|
| Starting point | One dataset and one established method | Verified anchor-paper reproduction plus meaningful baselines |
| Contribution | Reliable pipeline, fair comparison and one focused ablation | New mechanism, protocol, graph/view construction or rigorous transfer/robustness study |
| Evidence | Correct split, sensible baselines and error analysis | Multiple seeds, uncertainty, matched budgets, ablations and resource reporting where relevant |
| Outcome | Explain whether and when the method helps | Answer a preregistered question; a controlled negative result is valid |

## Shared protocol for self-supervised projects

Every self-supervised or pretrained project should report these settings whenever they are meaningful:

1. **Frozen linear evaluation.** Pretrain without labels, freeze the encoder and train only a lightweight head.
2. **Fine-tuning.** Initialise from the pretrained encoder and update it with labels.
3. **Fully supervised baseline.** Train the same encoder architecture from scratch using labels.
4. **Random-initialisation control.** Freeze a randomly initialised encoder and train the same head.
5. **Label-efficiency curve.** Report several label budgets, typically 1%, 5%, 10% and 100%.

::: {.leakage-callout}
**Leakage rule.** Group splits by the real independent unit: subject, patient, household, engine or bearing—never by window. On graphs, state whether pretraining is transductive or strict inductive. On forecasting tasks, preserve chronological order.
:::
